subject: the inside of a crowded apothecary cabinet seen head on and close, shelf above shelf filling the frame edge to edge with ranked glass specimen jars and squat stoppered bottles, their glass clouded and ringed with old residue and their blank paper labels peeling, and standing in that liquid the things the cabinet keeps, a two-headed lamb foetus, coiled pale snakes, a jar of loose human teeth, finger bones laid out in rows, a small cracked skull with a hole bored in its crown, brass calipers and bundles of dried herbs and bone-handled instruments hung on the uprights between the shelves, cobweb and dust thick in every corner and on the near edge of the lowest shelf, every jar lit from behind by a hot saturated magenta light, deep pink and violet shading to crimson, so the liquid glows and the specimens and the shelf boards read as silhouette, deep shadow between and behind the jars
